texts: good. one village-level burning event with the village's dead as what is burned, and no kind invented for them beyond what the words say.
good. the denial ranges over graves as a kind, so nothing asserts a grave into existence, and "no" is recorded as the quantifier word.
good. the surge, the displaced old graveyard, the Sunken Cove as destination and "six generations ago" as a measured gap back from now are all there.
good. the cremating event carries the pyre-shelf as its place and the shelf sits on the southern cliff, each relation on its own head.

mixed: everything is right except that "the ashes" was typed as a single individual of kind ash rather than as a set, which predicates ash-hood of the collection instead of its contents. The plural is what triggers it, so the mass wording parses cleanly as written: "The villagers scatter the ash at sea on the next ebb tide."
